thread:
Samir Patel: ran a quick CPU-side perf sampling + stack-unwind over a 5m run on the staging batcher (lots of short seq requests). attached collapsed stacks. tl;dr: large time in PyThread_acquire_lock -> tokenize_next -> memcpy -> scheduler.spin_wait. looks like GIL + tokenization + KV miss path interaction.

Maya S: can you paste the exact perf commands and kernel-selection config you ran? also which batching heuristics were enabled?

Samir Patel: sure, ran this on a dedicated vm and staging container to compare. commands:
```
perf record -F 99 -g --call-graph dwarf -o perf.data ./runner --mode=staging --profile 
perf script > out.collapsed
./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl out.collapsed > stacks.folded
./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl stacks.folded > flame.svg
```
kernel_selector=auto, batching=min_latency, kv_prefetch=off (defaults for the test).

Li Chen: looked at flame.svg, tokenizer is dominating for short requests but there is a clear C-Python boundary hotspot (PyThread_acquire_lock / PyEval_EvalFrameEx). also seeing context-switch spikes aligned with KV fetch RPCs. link: <internal-s3>/flames/1728456789/flame.svg

Janet (oncall): is this reproducible on the dedicated perf machines? staging containers add a lot of jitter. did you capture any perfetto/nsys traces to correlate with GPU kernel stalls?

PerfBot: Perf job 1728456789 completed. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1728456789/perf.data, s3://redwood-perf/1728456789/stacks.folded

Samir Patel: yes reproduced on a dedicated VM (1h run). forcing kernel_selector=static_int8 reduced CPU time ~12% because postproc callbacks are faster and fewer Python callbacks get invoked. interestingly when kv_prefetch=on we reduce context-switches but increase latency variance (probably contention). i'll open a small PR to try reducing tokenizer GIL hold.

Maya S: quick idea: move byte->token mapping build out of GIL or into a C extension that releases the GIL. pseudo-diff: 
```diff
- Py_BEGIN_ALLOW_THREADS
- // heavy loop that touches shared structures
- Py_END_ALLOW_THREADS
+ // implement in C: build_map_no_gil(buf, out)
+ // call from python with GIL held only for handoff
```
If we can do the hot path without the GIL we should see scheduler spin drop.

Samir Patel: plan: 1) add microbenchmark to measure tokenizer hold time per request (script attached in artifacts). 2) prototype a tiny C-extension that performs decode/tokenize without holding the GIL. 3) run A/B on dedicated pool and capture perf + perfetto for scheduler wakeups. i'll file an issue with steps and attach the artifacts.

Li Chen: ping me when the microbenchmark is up; i'll run perf + perfetto to capture sched wakeups (i suspect the scheduler spin/wakeup around queue head is amplifying the GIL stalls). happy to help with the C extension review. :thumbsup:

Samir Patel: thanks — i'll post the perf artifacts + PR link in this thread when ready. expected follow-ups: microbenchmark results, PR with C-ext prototype, perf + perfetto traces for A/B run.
